title: Session-based volatility/range prediction on XAUUSD H1
problem_statement: Predict next-session realized range/ATR (not return direction) using volatility clustering, to feed vol-aware position sizing.
mathematical_formulation: Let F_session(t) be a feature vector computed from the current session's volatility, range, and liquidity proxies. Target y = next_session_atr_pct = ATR_{t+1} / Close_t. H0: IC(F_session, y) = 0 after purged CV and walk-forward validation. H1: volatility clustering yields measurable predictive edge for next-session range.
author: RIDGE DELA TORJAGBO
notes:
Reframed from legacy HYP-B-001 (London morning -> overlap direction). New target is next-session ATR% for volatility forecasting. GARCH(1,1) is the mandatory baseline — XGBoost must beat GARCH on out-of-sample range prediction to justify complexity.

GARCH-ATR CONVERSION (required before comparison): GARCH(1,1) forecasts conditional variance of log returns (σ²_t). Target is next_session_atr_pct = ATR_{t+1}/Close_t. These measure different quantities (close-to-close return vol vs. intrabar high-low range). Conversion: (a) Fit GARCH(1,1) on training data; (b) forecast 1-step-ahead conditional variance σ²_{t+1|t}; (c) convert to daily vol forecast σ_{daily} = sqrt(σ²_{t+1|t} * 24) for H1 bars (24 H1 bars/day); (d) scale to ATR-equivalent using historical calibration factor k = median(ATR_t / (Close_t * σ_{daily,t})) computed on training set only; (e) GARCH_ATR_pct_forecast = k * σ_{daily} * Close_t. This k is fixed at train time and applied to val/test — no re-estimation. Alternative: use Parkinson/Garman-Klass range-based GARCH (CARR) instead of return-based GARCH; document which is used.

LEAKAGE CONTROLS (enforced in feature code):
- session:current_session_range = range of the MOST RECENTLY COMPLETED session only (e.g., at 13:00 UTC, range of London 08:00-12:00; Asia 00:00-07:00 already complete). No partial-session data.
- realized_vol_trailing_5/_20: rolling window of COMPLETED sessions only. At session boundary S_t, trailing window covers S_{t-5}..S_{t-1} (5 prior complete sessions). Never includes the target session S_{t+1} nor the current in-progress session.
- Features computed at session CLOSE timestamp, labels from NEXT session — strict no-lookahead.

SESSION DEFINITIONS (UTC, DST-aware via fixed offsets):
- Asia:      00:00–08:00 UTC  (Tokyo 09:00–17:00 JST, no DST)
- London:    08:00–17:00 UTC  (London 08:00–17:00 GMT/BST — uses fixed UTC offset, not local time)
- New York:  13:00–22:00 UTC  (NY 08:00–17:00 EDT/EST — fixed UTC offset)
- Overlap (London/NY): 13:00–17:00 UTC
- Session assignment per H1 bar: bar timestamp is the END of the bar (e.g., 08:00 bar covers 07:00–08:00). A bar belongs to session S if its END timestamp falls in S's UTC window.
